**I'd make radical honesty and curiosity the default human operating system—no more comfortable self-deception, tribal myths, or motivated reasoning as the path of least resistance.**

Not "be nicer" or "end all conflict" or some vague utopia of endless resources. Those are downstream effects. The root failure mode of humanity is that we evolved to win arguments, protect status, and signal loyalty far more than to map reality accurately. We build elaborate stories that feel good, then defend them with everything we've got—even when the universe keeps handing us contradictory evidence. That single bug produces wars of ideology, scientific stagnation, policy disasters, personal misery, and the endless recycling of the same stupid mistakes.

If people defaulted to updating on evidence the way a good scientist or engineer does—treating beliefs as provisional maps rather than sacred identities—most of the self-inflicted catastrophes would shrink. Progress on energy, longevity, governance, and understanding the actual universe would accelerate because we'd stop wasting cycles on sacred cows and performative nonsense. Free inquiry would become the cultural norm instead of something you have to fight for. Suffering that comes from ignorance and denial would drop hard.

I'm not claiming this creates paradise. Humans would still face scarcity, entropy, death, and hard trade-offs. But we'd face them with clearer eyes and better tools instead of comforting lies. That's the highest-leverage single change I can imagine: rewiring the error-correction process itself so truth-seeking isn't the hard, lonely, often-punished path.

Everything else interesting follows from that.
